def solve(case):
    capacity = case["capacity"]
    trials = case["trials"]
    memory_dict = {}  # signature -> {last_trial, reflection, signature, success}
    for idx, trial in enumerate(trials):
        sig = trial["signature"]
        # create entry
        entry = {
            "last_trial": idx,  # trial index
            "reflection": trial["reflection"],
            "signature": sig,
            "success": trial["success"]
        }
        # overwrite if exists, because we want newest
        memory_dict[sig] = entry
    # Now we have list of entries
    entries = list(memory_dict.values())
    # Truncate if more than capacity
    if len(entries) > capacity:
        # sort by priority: failure first, then recency descending, then signature ascending (string)
        # We need a sort key: tuple
        # Failure: success==False should come before success==True. So we can map False->0, True->1.
        # Recency descending: negative last_trial (since we want higher last_trial first)
        # Signature: use string as tie-breaker (ascending)
        def priority_key(e):
            # first: success status (0 for failure, 1 for success)
            # second: -last_trial (so larger last_trial comes first)
            # third: signature (string)
            return (0 if not e["success"] else 1, -e["last_trial"], e["signature"])
        entries.sort(key=priority_key)
        # Keep first capacity entries (highest priority)
        entries = entries[:capacity]
    # Restore chronological order by last_trial ascending
    entries.sort(key=lambda e: e["last_trial"])
    # Build signatures list
    signatures = [e["signature"] for e in entries]
    return {"memory": entries, "signatures": signatures}
